Injection 3 already achieved the maximum CRF of 1.000. Halve its gradient duration while keeping composition and temperature fixed to test whether its resolution margin permits a faster fully resolved separation.

Keep the fast gradient from injection 9 and lower temperature to improve the critical early-pair selectivity, which was stronger in cooler scouting runs. This tests whether full resolution can be restored while retaining a shorter separation than injection 3.

Raise phi1 one grid step to accelerate the last peak, which eluted during the final hold in injection 10. Keep the successful temperature and starting composition fixed while testing whether the early pair retains R ≥ 1.5 under the slightly steeper gradient.

Raise phi1 to shorten the last peak’s hold-phase retention, while lowering temperature one step to offset the expected loss of early-pair resolution from the steeper gradient. This targets a faster separation while preserving the maximum CRF already achieved.

Increase phi1 one step to shorten the last peak’s hold-phase retention, keeping all other settings from injection 12 fixed. The early pair’s R of 1.60 provides a small margin to test whether this faster method maintains full resolution and CRF 1.000.

Lower phi0 one step to test whether stronger initial retention restores the early pair above R = 1.5. Keep the high endpoint and short gradient from injection 13 to target full resolution with the last peak still near 3 minutes.

Lowering phi0 worsened the early pair, suggesting gradient steepness dominates in this range. Raise phi0 to 0.20 to make the gradient shallower while retaining the high endpoint, targeting R ≥ 1.5 with the last peak near 2.9 minutes.

Shift both gradient endpoints upward one step, preserving the slope that gave full resolution in injection 15 while accelerating late elution. This tests whether the early pair remains sufficiently retained and resolved at the higher starting organic fraction.

Raise phi0 one step to narrow the gradient window and shorten late retention while keeping the favorable low-temperature selectivity. This tests whether the early pair retains full resolution as it moves closer to the solvent front.

Raise temperature one step from injection 17 to shorten retention while testing the early pair’s resolution margin of 1.77. Keep the gradient unchanged to isolate the temperature effect and seek a faster method that preserves CRF 1.000.

Increase temperature one more grid step to locate the speed–resolution boundary for this gradient. The early pair is already close to the threshold at R = 1.58, so retain injection 18 as the fastest fully resolved fallback if resolution drops below 1.5.

Return to the successful 30 C temperature and raise phi0 one step to test a narrower, faster gradient window. This probes whether reduced gradient steepness can preserve early-pair resolution despite weaker initial retention; injection 18 remains the fastest fully resolved fallback.

Lower phi0 from injection 18 to keep the early peaks farther from the solvent front, and lower phi1 equally to preserve gradient steepness. This targets another maximum-CRF method with stronger initial retention and only a small increase in late-peak retention.

Reduce phi1 one step from the fastest fully resolved method, injection 18, to make the gradient shallower and improve the critical early-pair resolution margin. This targets another CRF 1.000 method with only a modest increase in last-peak retention.

Lower temperature one step from injection 22 to strengthen early-pair selectivity while keeping the separation short. Since CRF 1.000 is already achieved, this tests a nearby maximum-score method with a larger resolution margin; injection 18 remains the fastest fully resolved method observed.

Lower temperature from injection 21 to improve its marginal early-pair resolution while retaining a short run and keeping the first peak away from the solvent front. This targets another maximum-CRF method; injection 18 remains the fastest fully resolved method observed.

Narrow the gradient from injection 21 to improve its critical early-pair resolution while keeping all peaks well within 10 minutes. This final untested method targets CRF 1.000 with additional resolution margin; injection 18 remains the fastest fully resolved method observed.
